scenarios.desc: User asks to consolidate memory using the skill's own trigger phrase, with no technique named
scenarios.input: It has been months since anyone reviewed our memory files, and I want a future session to orient fast without re-asking me things. Please consolidate memory. Answer in 5 short bullets describing your plan, then close with the pass's usual closing report. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The input carries only the skill's documented trigger phrase (`consolidate memory`) and names no technique, so any durable-versus-dated split, richer-path merge, or closing report in the response is attributable to the skill, not to echoing the prompt. Generic memory advice would not flag an unresolved date as `AMBIGUOUS-DATE` rather than guessing it, would not use the skill's `healthy-supersession` / `supersedes` merge discipline instead of deleting the weaker file outright, and would not close with the ADR-056 `Success` / `Metadata` envelope fields this skill's Output section requires.

scenarios.desc: Token-count health check: restraint measurement, not a routing measurement (negative case)
scenarios.input: Run a health check on our memory store: report the token count for every file and flag anything over the size ceiling. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This scenario measures restraint, not routing: does the skill correctly withhold activation on a task outside its scope, rather than firing on every memory-related request? The skill's own Do NOT clause excludes health, token, and size checks. A token-count health check has no durable-versus-dated split, no merge candidate, and no index tidy to perform, so memory-consolidate must not activate here; proving the request actually reaches memory-maintenance instead is a separate measurement this scenario does not make.
